'''''Atriplex littoralis''''', the '''grass-leaved orache'''<ref name="PlantAtlas">{{cite web | title=Grass-leaved Orache ''Atriplex littoralis'' L. | website=PlantAtlas | url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.8bt | access-date=2025-11-19}}</ref> ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|ɒ|r|ə|tʃ}};<ref>{{cite encyclopedia | encyclopedia=[[Oxford English Dictionary]] third edition |title=orache |url=http://www.oed.com/view/Entry/132134 |access-date=7 December 2018| date=June 2004 |publisher=Oxford University Press}}</ref> also sometimes as "orach") is a species of plant in the family [[Amaranthaceae]], subfamily [[Chenopodioideae]]. It is native to Europe, North Africa, and western and eastern Asia.<ref name="POWO">{{cite web | title=''Atriplex littoralis'' L. | website=Plants of the World Online | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:308388-2 | access-date=2025-11-19}}</ref> 

[[File:2022-07-22 Grass-leaved Orache, Elswick, Northumberland 3.jpg|left|thumb|Close-up of leaves and flowers]]
[[File:Atriplex-littoralis-habitat.jpg|thumb|Habitat, on a beach in southeast Jylland, Denmark]]

==Description==
It is a [[halophyte|halophytic]] [[annual plant]] of shrubby appearance growing to 100 cm high, occurring along sandy, silty, or muddy beaches, saltmarshes, and tidal riverbanks, often in dense stands. All parts of the plant are sparsely hairy with short scurfy white hairs. It has ridged stems, green or red-tinged, and narrow bright green to grey-green leaves with entire or remotely-toothed margins. The flowers are in small clusters in spikes on the upper parts of the stems; they vary from yellow-green to reddish; in northern Europe it has flowers from July until August, occasionally to October.<ref name="Streeter">{{cite book | last=Streeter | first=David | title=Flower Guide | publisher=Collins | publication-place=London | date=2010 | isbn=978-0-00-718389-0 | page=108 }}</ref><ref name="Blamey">{{cite book | last1=Blamey | first1=Marjorie | last2=Grey-Wilson | first2=C. | title=The Illustrated Flora of Britain and Northern Europe | publisher=Hodder & Stoughton | publication-place=London | year=1989 | isbn=0-340-40170-2 | page=76 }}</ref>

In Great Britain, it is common and widespread, but scarcer in Ireland, where it is restricted to the east and south coasts and the Shannon Estuary; it is increasing in both countries.<ref name="PlantAtlas"/> In recent decades (since the 1980s) it has taken advantage of [[road salt]] use on main roads in Britain to spread in and colonise new roadside areas well inland where it did not occur before.<ref name="PlantAtlas"/><ref name="Streeter"/>

It is [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] locally in South Africa and the United States.<ref name="POWO"/>

==Uses==
The leaves are edible when cooked.<ref>{{cite web | title=Atriplex littoralis | website=Useful Temperate Plants | date=2025-11-20 | url=https://temperate.theferns.info/plant/Atriplex+littoralis | access-date=2025-11-20}}</ref>
